title: New US licence rules on advanced AI chip shipments
what_happened: A US Commerce Department rule in effect from 2026-11-19 requires licences for advanced chips going to overseas data centres that give significant computing access to companies from restricted countries, and for advanced-node chips made for non-approved designers. Press reports, not yet confirmed here, say TSMC and Samsung suspended some shipments to Chinese customers pending licences.
how_it_reaches_markets: Lost or delayed sales for chip makers and equipment makers; retaliation risk; adds to pressure on AI-linked shares.

sourced_facts.text: Interim final rule 'Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors' (Bureau of Industry and Security), effective on publication, scheduled for 2026-11-19: adds a licence requirement for advanced-node chips from non-approved designers exported by a front-end fabricator or packaging firm, and for exports to overseas data centres that give significant compute access to companies headquartered in restricted countries

The same rule requires a licence for advanced chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, with an exclusion for US-headquartered end users; comments are due 60 days after publication
Background: a final rule published 2026-01-15 had moved certain advanced computing chips for China and Macau from presumption of denial to case-by-case licence review

resolved_when_all: The rules are published in final form with licence criteria, AND at least one major supplier publicly confirms that suspended shipments have resumed under licence
worsened_when_any: China announces retaliatory export or import restrictions citing the rules
The rules are widened to cover additional chip categories or countries

relief_headlines_that_do_not_resolve_it: Reports that licences 'will be granted' without confirmed resumed shipments

history.note: Card opened. Resolution conditions written before the outcome is known.

Sources upgraded in part. Only the January 2026 rule has been read at the primary source. The November 2026 rule is known so far only through a wire reprint, which gives an effective date of 2026-11-19; the Federal Register text is still to be found. The reprint is not listed as a source under the source rule.

Second pass. The November rule was found and read: an interim final rule of the Bureau of Industry and Security, effective on publication on 2026-11-19. The earlier note that the rule text had not been located no longer applies.

Summary rewritten so that it states only what was confirmed at the listed sources and marks the rest as reported. The first version is kept under superseded_sources. Resolution conditions are unchanged.

note: Risk state only. Not a forecast and not investment advice.
unconfirmed_facts: TSMC suspending some orders at 16 nm and below unless customers obtain licences; FT report that TSMC and Samsung suspended some shipments: read only in a wire reprint dated 2026-11-20
ASML and Infineon share falls: not confirmed

superseded_sources.reason: Source rule of 2026-11-26: at least one primary source per card; commentary, blogs and reposts are not used as support
facts_as_first_written: Commerce Department announcement in the week ending 2026-11-20; exact date not stated in source (T. Rowe Price)
FT: TSMC and Samsung suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers pending US licences; Reuters: TSMC halting certain advanced-node orders (both as cited by T. Rowe Price)
ASML and Infineon shares fell on concerns over tighter US chip export restrictions (T. Rowe Price)
superseded_sources.summary_as_first_written: The US Commerce Department announced rules requiring licences for certain shipments of advanced AI chips to overseas data centers that provide substantial computing power to specified Chinese entities. Press reports say TSMC and Samsung Electronics suspended some shipments to Chinese customers pending licences.

condition_reading_notes.note: How the conditions above are read. The conditions themselves are unchanged.
notes: The rule is an interim final rule already in effect. 'Published in final form' counts when the Bureau of Industry and Security publishes a final rule after the comment period or states that the interim rule stands. 'Major supplier' means TSMC or Samsung.
